parts.text: Which claim correctly treats a force as a push or pull between two objects?

options.text: Alok pushes a door — a push between his hand and the door.
A notebook rests on a desk — the notebook applies a force to itself.
Imran pulls a suitcase — the pull acts only on the suitcase.
A raindrop falls — no objects are interacting.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Sonia studies four events: Alok pushes a classroom door with his hand; a notebook rests on a desk; Imran pulls a suitcase; a raindrop falls.

part_answers.answer: A force is a push or pull between two objects; the push names the pair of hand and door.

teacher.key_rationale: A force is a push or pull between two objects. The door push names that pair. A notebook does not push itself. A pull is between Imran and the suitcase, not only on the suitcase. A falling raindrop still interacts with Earth.
